What US adults measure is higher: an average of 38.7% for women and 27.2% for men aged 20 to 59 (our calculation from CDC body scans, 2011–2018)."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "What is the lowest body fat a woman can have?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "CDC’s scans show how low US women measure: of 5,462 women aged 20 to 59, 1 in 100 measured under 23.3% body fat and 1 in 20 under 27.2% (our calculation, 2011–2018). On the provisional ranges, body fat under 21% at ages 20 to 39 (under 23% at 40 to 59) is “low”: the level that goes with an underweight BMI (Gallagher et al., 2000)."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Is 30% body fat chubby?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "It depends on sex. For a woman, 30% is inside the provisional healthy range at 20 to 39 (21–32.9%), and 85% of US women that age measured more. For a man, 30% is above the range at every age: “very high” starts at 25% at 20 to 39, 28% at 40 to 59 and 30% at 60 to 79 (Gallagher et al., 2000). Still, 29% of US men aged 20 to 39 measured more than 30% (our calculation from CDC body scans)."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Is 20% body fat skinny?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "Not for a man: 20% is the start of the provisional “high” range at 20 to 39 and inside the healthy range at 40 to 59 (11–21.9%), and 82% of US men aged 20 to 39 measured more. For a woman, 20% is under the provisional healthy range (it starts at 21% at 20 to 39), and more than 99% of US women aged 20 to 39 measured more (our calculation from CDC body scans)."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "What’s a good body fat index?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "“Body fat index” isn’t one fixed measure. If you mean body fat percentage, the share of body weight that is fat, the provisional healthy ranges are 21–32.9% for women and 8–19.9% for men aged 20 to 39, a little higher with age (Gallagher et al., 2000). If you mean the body mass index (BMI), weight divided by height squared, the healthy range is 18.5 to 24.9 (CDC). There is also a fat mass index: fat mass in kilograms divided by height in meters squared."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Is 20% body fat realistic?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "For men, yes: 18.2% of US men aged 20 to 39 measured 20% or less in CDC’s scans. For women it is rare: 0.3% of women aged 20 to 39 measured 20% or less (our calculation, 2011–2018)."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Is 18% body fat chubby?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "No. For a man, 18% is inside the provisional healthy range at every age from 20 to 79, and 89% of US men aged 20 to 39 measured more. For a woman, 18% is under the provisional healthy range; only 0.1% of US women aged 20 to 39 measured 18% or less (our calculation from CDC body scans)."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Is 140 pounds fat for a 5′4″ female?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "Not by BMI. At 5′4″, 140 lb is a BMI of 24.0, inside CDC’s healthy range of 18.5 to 24.9; the healthy weight at that height runs up to 145 lb (CDC categories). Body fat varies a lot at the same BMI: US women aged 20 to 59 with a BMI of 23.5 to 24.4 measured a median 35.5% body fat, and the middle half were between 33.0% and 38.2% (our calculation from CDC body scans, 2011–2018)."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "What is the average body fat percentage?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "38.7% for US women and 27.2% for US men aged 20 to 59, measured with DXA scans in CDC’s 2011–2018 surveys (our calculation). By age it runs from 36.9% for women in their 20s to 40.3% in their 50s, and from 25.4% to 28.3% for men."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Why is there no data for people over 60?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "CDC’s whole-body DXA scans in 2011–2018 covered ages 8 to 59 only (CDC). For ages 60 to 79 the chart shows the provisional ranges, not US measurements."}}]}]} </script>
